texts.text: Ah... At last, to be graced with the sweet release from the gaol that was the restroom...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Fuhu, hello there~
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: *sigh* ... What pity! Verily, the madness of boredom spareth not even young Hong Lu in its merciless rampage, for he hath begun to converse with the very world outside the restroom...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I too, in search of excitement, had attempted to engage in a contest of staring with the wordless lady... Yet of all 10 bouts, I failed to seize even a single victory... Tedium is indeed a formidable adversary, for it confuseth the mind to make fellows out of the very air... Hmm hmm...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Ah, I wasn't saying hello to the air, Don Quixote! We have a new friend with us, see?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Would you kindly introduce us, Dante?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: A-ah, quite true. It appeareth that the little bairn is on our heels... Whoever might they be?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: They are someone we picked up on the second floor. Our current objective is to bring them to the fifth floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: "Picked up" a child, thou sayest...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: There was a mutual consent of unspoken nature.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <The Rouges requested that we bring them to the fifth floor...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ooh, a request, thou sayest? This be a contract, then! Well met, I am Don Quixote! 'Tis my dream to become the best Fixer there is! And whoever might thou be?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Ahh...
W-whomst...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Uuh... eeh...
Hmm...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Ahh...
Ahh...
Eh, Manager Esquire? Wouldst thou do the honors of introduction...? I would much like to call this child by a name, though they might not speak their own...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <H-huh, we never asked their name...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Hoh?! Hast thou traveled so long with this child and thought not to ask their name!? Pray, just what have you been calling this child thus far?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: That's a bit insensitive, Dante. They're someone who'll be coming along with us on this journey—the least we could do is try to learn their name, even if it's only for a short while.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <The Brand Director... didn't tell us the kid's name...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <U-uhm, what should I call this kid? Should we name them?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Hmm... Why don't we ask them? Even children who are still learning how to speak sometimes know how to pronounce their own names.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... That is a reasonable conjecture.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: We would like you to tell us your name.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Buu...
Pwuh...
texts.speaker: Pwuh...

texts.text: Pwie...
texts.speaker: Pwuh-Pwuhie...

texts.text: Aha! What an adorable name you have~
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I think their name is Pwie, Dante.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Oooh, what a whimsical name thou hast, young Pwie!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <Uhm... Are you sure that's their full name?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Such narrow-mindedness! Expand the horizons of thy mind, Manager Esquire, for all names are noble and worthy of their breaths!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <Yeah, yeah... Thanks for the lecture.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ahem! I welcome thee with open arms into our adventuring party, young Pwie!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I must warn thee afore we are to proceed: the journey ahead shall be fraught with danger! Yet worry thee not—for no matter the hardship, I, Don Q—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... Wherefore is it that thou standest at such a distance, young Pwie?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Uu...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <I think they're afraid...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Afraid? Wherefore?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <... I think they're just wary of us in general.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: But... from what I've been able to see from our brief journey from the second to the fourth floor, I think the people Pwie was most afraid of... are Meursault and me.
Ooooh... 'Tis as though we have walked through a portal into another world.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hast thou any thoughts to share, young Pwie? Hie thee here, here! Ooooh... Hoooh...! What other wondrous curiosities await in this department store, I wonder?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Lean any closer, and you might end up eating the shoe, Don Quixote.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Ahem, 'tis but a close inspection, nothing more...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: What a disgrace you are, Four-legs. You were entrusted with but one duty—one—the shop's cleanliness. Yet I see that you've failed spectacularly at that simple task.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: I have indeed failed you, honorable One-leg. I couldn't carry out that simple duty on account of my stupidity and idleness.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: There is a reason you are made to drag those unsightly legs with you, Four-legs. Remind yourself of that with every step you take.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: ... I understand, One-leg. My deepest apologies.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Forgive that shameful display, dear customer. Lowly though I am, I will now attend to you instead. ... Should you tolerate my vulgar presence, of course.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Is... is all well? That one-legged woman seemed to be bullying thee quite harshly.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: In the sartorial arts, a shoe is an article of clothing wrought to meet the ground and spare the body from the impurities of dirt. The fewer the feet that touch the ground, the nobler the being—and the more exalted the purpose of the lone shoe.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: As our names suggest, lowly Four-legs like myself walk the earth with too many appendages...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: The universal aspiration of the Footwear Hall employees is to ascend into a higher state of being—"One-leg," whose sheer existence is balanced proudly upon a single leg.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: W-well... If thou sayest so... Then what must one do to become a... "One-leg"?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Craft shoes with tireless devotion. Sell them in faithfulness. Discipline the body so that fewer and fewer feet may tread upon the ground. Perseverance and persistence shall be our salvation—
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: You must all be quite new to this floor, if you're still asking questions like that.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Yes, we are. We came up from the floors below.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: From the— You're from downstairs...? Then might you be the customers everyone is whispering about...? The customers who are unbound to the floors...?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Mm. We can travel between floors without restriction.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I... see. The rumors were true. Only rumors are allowed to travel between each floor of this department store, so we never know whether they're true or false.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Then... could you confirm the veracity of another rumor for me?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Hm, what rumor would that be?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: It used to be that the customers of the Grand Magasin who collapsed could rise again on the lower floors. However many times they collapsed, they could begin anew from the very start.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Yet ever since the day the cracks formed on the walls... I hear that collapsed customers no longer rise—not just here, but on the lower floors, too.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Is there any... grain of truth to that?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: It is true. Revival is no longer possible here.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Not true.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <Pwie...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: You can get up again. No one wantsta... just lie on a cold floor in the end.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: You can wake up again... after you collapse.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: It almost came off as a stubborn child's insistence, but...
... there was a nameless confidence in Pwie's voice, as though they were certain that it would come true.
Ah... Then... will I awaken again on B1, as we always have...?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: ... Mhm.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: I've always had so much admiration for the One-legs... and their magnificent stance as they pushed themselves against the earth with but the strength of a single leg, the whole of their existence concentrated upon a singular point. But it was always out of my reach, no matter how hard I labored.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Then... I want to start from the beginning again.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Your voice feels... terrifying and uncanny, unlike the Voice that speaks to me. But... you must be someone strong and prestigious...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: ... So collapse me, won't you? So I can start anew, from the beginning...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Ah... It's all... fading away...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: When I wake... I'll see the... blue skies... again...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Were you telling him the truth?
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... I dunno. But... I want it to be true.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Surprisingly enough, that little thing is telling the truth.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Ever since it was born, the great cycle that had once disappeared from the Grand Magasin... has returned.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>I suppose B1 will be filled with shells again. Shells housing soft, supple beings.</color>
Ooh... this be the voice of young Meursault's lover, Lady Jeanne?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Fuhu, that's me. Ex-lover, to clarify. Hey, ma puce... I don't always have to be your ex-something, if you ever change your mind.</color>
After all, we haven't had real closure yet, hm?
Voice...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Oh yes, I am a Voice. Perfect and complete, unlike you.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>The Rouges seem to have high hopes for you, but... I don't know.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>I'm afraid you're way too tiny to hold up this crumbling department store. Even the Golden Bough's barely keeping it standing.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Raise it well, ma puce.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Though I doubt that little thing could change how this ends.</color>
... So, according to Miss Jeanne... the Golden Bough is the last thing holding the Grand Magasin together.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Then... what would happen to this place if we removed it?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hm... Verily, the "resin" sealing the fissures would disappear... whereupon the collapse of the department store would surely follow...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hoh... Would not the liberation of incarcerated N Corp. residents be within reach, then?! 'Twould be a most fortuitous outcome!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... A foolish, ignorant death... Perfectly befitting a Four-legs.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: It never understood the natural order that governs the Footwear Hall. The cycle in which the sole purpose of the Four-legs' base existence is to elevate us One-legs to be revered.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: ... But why?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Why do they revere you just 'cuz you have fewer legs?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Because only a One-leg such as myself can achieve the magnificent stance where I push myself against the earth with but the strength of a single leg.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Pwie lifted a leg off the ground and stared at One-leg.
I have two legs. But I'm standing on one leg.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: That's... that's not magnificent. Imperfect.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Standing on one leg's... uncomfy.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: She doesn't know what to say—you must've hit a nerve, Pwie.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: The number of our legs is a symbol of divine providence in the Footwear Hall, and a natural law by which we have abided since time immemorial.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Don't you dare meddle with our tradition, you foul, revolting Rouge-spawn. Same goes for you as well, strangers.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: That wasn't a very nice thing to say.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: You might want to apologize to Pwie.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hong Lu's mouth straightened into a thin line, the cheerful smile that so often graced his lips gone without a trace. The One-leg's tirade seemed to have genuinely offended him.
I'm... foul and... revolting...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... Yes, you are. I barely stopped myself from retching the moment I saw you, you disgusting little vermin.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: I dunno.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: The lady downstairs, she... was happy to see me. Praised me.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: And you... think I'm disgusting. Hating me from the moment we met.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: But... I'm still me. Same me as I was downstairs. Why am I different to you?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: You really are an infuriating little thing, aren't you? Question after question about things that are so obvious...
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: But fine, I'll grace you with the truth. The only reason anyone would ever be glad to see you is that they're the Rouges—a rotten and avaricious sort.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: You know what? Why am I even subjecting myself to this useless drivel? I'll shut that impudent mouth for good.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: We gave you a chance to say nice things, but... I don't think you're going to take it at this point.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Young Pwie, though our foe was in the wrong, for she hath spewed such venomous and unjust tirade against thee...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I must advise thee against answering questions with questions, no matter how curious thou mayest be—for doing so in excess may sow the seeds of trouble.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Though curiosity is indeed a commendable quality, alas, there are times when one must exercise restraint.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: But why...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Don Quixote briefly fell into a thousand-yard stare.
Though I may be speaking from naught else but mine experience, to ask question after question may invite young Heathcliff's bat to smack—mmmpph!!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... While that might be a reason...!
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... it's usually because some questions are, by their nature, troublesome to answer. You could hurt others' feelings by asking questions like that, and... even make things a little awkward.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... That's... weird.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Are "things" not allowed to be "awkward"?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: When people say that things are awkward, they mean that they're uncomfortable. Though we naturally want things to be relaxed and comfortable, some people want to achieve that peace without talking things through.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Those people tend to try to get there by forcing misunderstandings or by fighting the source of awkwardness to physically remove them.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Oh... I don't like that.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Fuhu, right?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: But... I don't know what questions are troublesome. And I still wanna ask 'cuz I'm curious.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: What should I do?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Hmmm~ Questions usually become troublesome when we don't want to raise a fuss, so... Ah, how about you raise your hand before asking something?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Too much work.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: I must admit, 'tis not a method that is always reciprocated... But with quiet persistence, a kind soul shall eventually espy thy persevering hand! A most wonderful method, wouldst thou not say?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Pwie considered Hong Lu's suggestion for a bit, cocking their head to the side... then raised a hand.
It wasn't long before they raised both of their hands...
... and having thought of a third—and possibly, a fourth, and a fifth too—question, began impatiently flapping their hands in the air.
Mm, not very handy. Need more hands, maybe.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: You only need to lift one hand, once. Any follow-up questions can be posed by subsequently raising your arm after the first query has been answered.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Aha...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Good idea. I think.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Another thing: If you have a question for me, it is unnecessary to raise your hand. When your question happens to be a troublesome sort, I will inform you directly.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Pwie nodded... then, their attention arrested by yet another curiosity, tottered toward the display cabinet Don Quixote was observing.
Hm? Did you see any shoes that you find to your liking?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Shoe...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Hoh...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Fie... Only now did I notice! Young Pwie, how is it that thou wearest not a shoe?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: To walk this earth bare of feet cannot be a pleasant experience, young Pwie... Is it not rough on thy skin...? And cold...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <Should we get them one...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We can purchase you a pair of shoes, if there is something you like.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... I don't like any of these. And I'm hungry.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: But... Shoes are nice. I want one...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <Hmm, maybe we should try taking them to a non-Noir shop...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Let's head down. I think the Rouges had a shop down there as well.
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What might this place be...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Looks like they sell furniture here.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Still so dark... and eerily quiet.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Moving to the last known location of the Happy Closet.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... H-AAAAARK!! Be thou the master of this hall?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: H-hark...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I wonder if they're unable to speak?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: As we approach, the one they call "Happy Closet" unfurl their body once again.
And just as we had seen before, there's an assortment of miscellany and parts of human anatomy dangling inside.
Hoh... Could this be... thy manner of parley? Ah, I see! Thou'rt flaunting thy colección, perchance?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Or... maybe they're asking us to take them with us.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I have conducted a thorough search, but there does not seem to be a "red heart shard" among their collection.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The shoe vendor did say that they are a giving soul... Maybe they gave it away already?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Maybe so, but...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... I think we're going to have to tear their heart out like the Furnishings did last time.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... There are many eyes on us, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Immediately attempting to remove the Happy Closet's heart will most likely provoke the Furnishings into attacking us.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <I really don't want to do this again, but... let's first distribute the Happy Closet's items to the Furnishings.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <They shouldn't have any problem with it then, right? The Furnishings get what they want, and we get to rip out the Happy Closet's heart... it's fair game for everyone.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: As we were discussing what to do with the Furnishings, Pwie tore off a few pieces of the Happy Closet's trinkets.
It seemed to me it was more out of curiosity than covetousness—Pwie watched the Happy Closet carefully, trying to see if they reacted in any way.
If you share... you'll be empty.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Are you... okay with becoming empty...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Pwie takes a few more items from their body, but they still don't stir. Only when we've walked a fair distance away from them do they fold themselves shut.
Th-this be a lamp, or this be a man? Forsooth, a pickle indeed...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hmm... that sure is a conundrum. Wouldn't that depend on how we look at it?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: You need only consider every entity here a customer, a product, a vendor, and a Mannequin all at once.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Alright... Let's start by giving this guy some clothes.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Hark, kind Sir!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Aha. Customers.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Will you... Will you purchase me?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Though my bent back may give you an impression of bad posture at first, it is in fact my strength—the subtle combination of height and angle ensures that any customer in search of respite will be most appropriately illuminated.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Ah, well. In truth, w-what we seek is—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I may creak a little—the last customer who inspected me was regrettably coarse with their hands. But worry you not. My functions are not one bit affected.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Come, feel the softness of my body. Why don't you try lighting me up now, young fellows?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: N-nay, worry thee not. In truth, 'tis simply that thou were the first to catch mine eye—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Caught your eye, did I?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Well, well, well... Isn't that encouraging to hear? It can only mean that I am clearly different in terms of composition compared to the rest of the common rabble on display here!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Perchance, that may be so. 'Tis quite blindingly bright where thou standest, indeed.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Someone with such a keen eye for aesthetic detail will surely be willing to purchase me, hmm?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I am yours for a very reasonable price of 4,000 eyeballs. Outrageously underpriced for the unmatched coziness my lighting provides, if I do say so myself.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: We are not here to purchase you. We are only here to distribute the articles of clothing taken from the Happy Closet to the residents of the Furniture Hall.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ah. You speak of the master of the Furniture Hall.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I don't even know if they carry anything that would go well with my style... Well, let's see what you've brought me.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Pwie spread out the clothes they were carrying in front of the floor lamp.
Erm...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Behold! Outfits chosen by the most discerning hands of young Pwie here!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I must say... this piece is not entirely consonant with my own aesthetic sense...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Ack!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... However, as you are all doubtlessly true aesthetes who have managed to recognize my overwhelming magnificence within the Furniture Hall... I trust that there was some apocryphal philosophy behind this choice of fashion. I will... wear it, I guess...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: You gave that rusty old lamp an outfit?! No fair, he's been outta fashion since forever, dudes! Do me too, do me too! Decorate me!
Dress me up, and I'll let you buy me at an affordable price!
He has it so good. Hardly any sunlight reaches us back here... Let us have something, too...

If you won't, then we'll...
If you won't, then we'll...
Be-becalm thyselves! All shall be distributed in good time!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <Let's head back to the Happy Closet, and... pick out some clothes.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: They're all...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... trying to wear something. Why...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Wherefore, thou askest? Why, 'tis to make one's heartbeat dash by donning an outfit most dashing!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: They are hoping to be pinned.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Wearing an outfit is at once an immediately identifiable method of self-expression and infixation.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Mm, quite an interesting verbiage thou hast chosen to explain how individualistic expression leads to electrifying excitement, young Meursault...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Don't you want to have clothes like they do, Pwie?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: No, what I want...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: What I want is...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Pwie trailed off, absorbed in thought.
As we approach, the one they call "Happy Closet" unfurl their body once again.
And just as we had seen before, there's an assortment of miscellany and parts of human anatomy dangling inside.
Hoh... Could this be... thy manner of parley? Ah, I see! Thou'rt flaunting thy colección, perchance?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Or... maybe they're asking us to take them with us.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I have conducted a thorough search, but there does not seem to be a "red heart shard" among their collection.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The shoe vendor did say that they are a giving soul... Maybe they gave it away already?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Maybe so, but...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... I think we're going to have to tear their heart out like the Furnishings did last time.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... There are many eyes on us, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Immediately attempting to remove the Happy Closet's heart will most likely provoke the Furnishings into attacking us.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <I really don't want to do this again, but... let's first distribute the Happy Closet's items to the Furnishings.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <They shouldn't have any problem with it then, right? The Furnishings get what they want, and we get to rip out the Happy Closet's heart... it's fair game for everyone.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: As we were discussing what to do with the Furnishings, Pwie tore off a few pieces of the Happy Closet's trinkets.
It seemed to me it was more out of curiosity than covetousness—Pwie watched the Happy Closet carefully, trying to see if they reacted in any way.
If you share... you'll be empty.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Are you... okay with becoming empty...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Pwie takes a few more items from their body, but they still don't stir. Only when we've walked a fair distance away from them do they fold themselves shut.
The Happy Closet, as the others called them, opens up to us once again.
So... I wonder what the other Furnishings are looking for?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hm... It shall be of our choosing. Good Closet, wouldst thou allow us to take several at once from thee?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The Happy Closet still does not stir.
<... I'm not entirely sure if it's a good idea to keep distributing clothes, considering what happened last time...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: If you would rather proceed using a more violent method—
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Nah. Let's not get into unnecessary fights when we have Pwie with us.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Why are you always giving things away...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Do you not have... wants?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Wanna have this...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... Closed. You don't like receiving things?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Why won't you talk? Frustrating.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Prithee, consider that their name is "Happy Closet!" Perchance acts of charity be what give them happiness!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Or maybe that "happiness" of the Happy Closet isn't theirs at all. Maybe it belongs to the other Furnishings.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: A given name is, after all... a culmination of wishes from those who gave it.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: What took you so long?! My bones're freezing from the lack of deco!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: A-apologies, good fellow, What is it that thou needst?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I want a toenail! Toenail on my hat! I'll look so classy with a toenail on my hat!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Toenail... This be the toenail thou seekest, perchance?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Heavens... Have you misplaced your eyes on the soles of your feet?! Try putting them where you can see!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: This looks like a toenail to you? It's obviously a tongue!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Ah...! Had I not shared much the same doubt with thee, Manager Esquire? Loath I be to say it, but thou truly hast no eye for the aesthetics of fashion!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: But... this is a pretty nice tongue, I'll give you that. It'll go quite well with my light.
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Oh boy, hope I'll sell for a high price...
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Do you... really need that?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Of course I do. I need this to sell at a premium.
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: After you sell at a premium... what then?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Wha—selling at a premium is a good thing in and of itself! That's what everyone says!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: *yawn* So sleepy...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Why do I gotta stay awake...?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Hello, what outfit would you like?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I mean, it's obvious, isn't it...? Something beautiful so someone'll buy me soon... Ah, I know... I want a warm and fuzzy coat, so I can snooze right back to sleep as soon as I'm sold...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Sure thing, here you go—
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... What do you want me to do with this? Drape it over me.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: You think I should be bothered to haul myself up to get dressed? Do you have any idea how sleepy I am?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: <... Same old, huh?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh, haha... Here you go. How's that?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: So nice... So nice. You can go.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: I'm gonna need some time to get used to this fuzzy coziness... I'll... uhm... give you a discount of 200 eyeballs when I'm fully acclimated. A token of my gratitude.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: You better purchase me, okay?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: You don't seem any different...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Shush your little mouth, kid. It's not like you were going to purchase me, anyway...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: I like that you're bringing me the good stuff willingly, my dudes.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: You guys must be the totally kewl~ kinda customers.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Thank you for your kind words. Here—which one would you like?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Guess what? I'm a totally kewl~ Furnishing, too. Yoink! Didn't even need to think.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: <Didn't even hesitate, huh...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: With that done, why don'tcha dudes be totally kewl~ too and buy me?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I'll give ya a discount of 300 eyeballs if you're kewl~ about it, how's that, my dudes?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I ask thee, in a manner most kewl~—what be thy price, with that most generous discount?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: It makes me a totes reasonable 3,600 eyeballs. Far out, huh? Oops, or am I lowballing myself?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Silence descended around us as we all struggled to come to terms with that ridiculous asking price.
Dang, not so kewl~ after all, huh?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: That's gonna be a no-go for me, my dudes. I want my buyer to be totally kewl~.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: What does it mean to be "kewl"...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: To be kewl~ is to be kewl~, no more, no less.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: It means to become cooler. More dashing, more admirable.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Really? Then you Furnishings aren't so kewl~.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Wearing something you've robbed from others...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Y'know, when you put it like that... Point taken. But I'm gonna be kewl~ and just smoove over it.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Really? This is all that's left inside the Closet?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Hmm... Kinda disappointing, guys.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Why didn't you come to me first before anyone else?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: We weren't avoiding you, if that's what you're saying. We just happened to visit everyone here in the order they caught our eye...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: *scoff* Are you implying that I'm not as eye-catching as the others?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Hmph! I know I'm on the somewhat petite side in this Hall, but there's no need to be so rude.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Forget it, I'm taking this.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: And don't think you'll be getting a good-bye OR a thank-you discount from me!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: That's too bad, then. We won't be able to afford you without a discount.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ...Hmph.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: S-see if I care! I bet someone way, way richer than you'll splurge for me soon!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: But you're still pretty unremarkable.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Why don't you just give it back to the owner? Not like it'll change anything.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... No way! You can't just take back a gift!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Thank you... Thank you ever so much for bringing me such a precious item.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: I hope this isn't an imposition, but... Oh, every garment you brought me is simply beautiful... I'll go with this one.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Mm.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: And this one...
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Aaaaand this one.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: One item per customer.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Ah, really?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Oh... I'm sorry, I must've gotten ahead of myself. The sunshine's been so warm lately, I feel like I'm floating.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: But don't you think it's rather heartless of you to throw me one miserable scrap of sacking and expect me to go over the rainbow?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: It's our policy.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Tsk. That's a stupid fucking policy, isn't it?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: The fuck're you lookin' at! Get lost, fuckwit!
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: ... Why is the couch so mad?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: It's not like it's doing us a favor. We're the ones giving, aren't we?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Because that couch thinks that they are entitled to our generosity.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Those who feel entitled... tend to forget that they ought to be grateful instead.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text:
Me this one!
This one!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Hmm.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text:
Wow!
Wow!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
Thankies!
Thankies!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: <Glad this is still easy, at least.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text:
Wanna buy me?
Buy me!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
9,900 eyeballs! A steal!
A steal!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Thine offer is the most exorbitant price we have heretofore encountered!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text:
Yep, yep!
Yep, yep!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
Cuz I'm awesome!
I'm awesome!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Alas, we have not with us such a grand sum of—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text:
What a bum!
What a bum!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: How cruel of thee...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Don't take it too personally, Don Quixote. We are a bit strapped for eyeballs at the moment.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Are we bums?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Fiiiieee... It burneth mine heart to be subjected to such derision... Young Pwie, I promise thee—though we may be ocularly disenfranchised, thou shan't grow up in an impoverished childhood...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <Really tugs at your heartstrings, huh...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... We need a heart shard. I request that you hand yours over to us.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The Happy Closet opens up without a word.
<Not that I expected them to be any different, but they don't hesitate to open up, even for a request like this...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Hm... Though the necessity of it leaves us no other option... it must be said that this leaves a discomforting rot in one corner of my chest.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: To lose one's heart is to lose one's life... And life is of greater import than even the preciously limited colección such as this...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: If you were in the same situation, would you willingly give up your collection of badges to help the people in need?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Mmm... If it be in service of helping the troubled, then I shall fain part with my entire colección—!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: —eeeeeeeehhhhhhhhh, though, mayhap thou wilt be merciful and spare the limited edition Red Mist commemorative badge? 'Twould leave me with naught but sorrow were I to be deprived of even that...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: What's a badge?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: They are remembrances bearing commemorative emblems of great Fixers; I wear them so that they may forever live on in mine heart.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Fixers...? Is that the Voice you follow?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Hmm... Fond of questions with no easy answers, art thou not? The one we "follow" at present is Manager Esquire, yet...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: You don't follow me, but you still wanna bring me to higher floors.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: What do you want?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: We pursue the enactment of justice! If there be downtrodden and troubled souls, we seek to assist them with nary a concern for how their woes came to be!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Strangers... You say a lotta complicated stuff.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: With all that said, you still don't follow me.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Oh, stop it with your pearl-clutching.
W-what is the meaning of this? A-and... ye were all mobile, all along?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <But we were more generous about it than we were last time... Was that not enough?!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: *yawn* Tried to get some shut-eye... but the sunshine kept me up.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: I'm going to need more than one article of clothing if I want someone to buy me before the sunshine grows even warmer.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Bet that closet's hiding even kewl~er goodies inside.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I bet they've got some luxury stuff hidden inside that you uncultured swines couldn't even recognize.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: I hope this isn't an imposition, but would you mind giving me everything you have?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text:
Want all of it!
All of it!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: W-wait, what—?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Move, move! Me first pick! Me first pick!!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: ... As we reel from the sudden turn of events, the Furnishings shove us aside and descend upon the motionless Happy Closet like a flock of carrion birds.
Their body remains unfurled even as they are knocked down to the ground.
*yawn*... Shame, Rocking Chair sold for 2,100 eyeballs. Would've been me had they not been wearing that newfangled scarf. Now they'll get to sleep forever—must be so, so very nice...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Keep dreaming, you greedy thing. You took the most clothes out of Happy Closet, you know?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Hope there's a cow-print shin somewhere in there... That'd be pretty kewl~ ya know?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: You bitch, that lower lip you just took is pretty much a set with the philtrum I chose!
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text:
Leave the eyebrows!
Leave the eyebrows!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Excuse me.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Oh? Hello, Mister Lamp. When did you...?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: You can get out of my way if you have no further business with the closet.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: What brazen sabotage... Looking to snatch away my potential customers, eh? I won't take it sitting down!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: <... What a pack of vultures.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: H-halt! Canst thou not see, that the Closet has naught left to give?! Cease this robbery this instant! Cease!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The Furnishings backed off a little at Don Quixote's urgent intervention,
but they continued to circle the fallen Happy Closet, greedily eyeing for an opportunity to snatch up more adornments that may or may not be there.
All of the Closet's possessions hath already been distributed fairly amongst thee.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Thus—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... Not fairly.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Wasn't fair. Curtain didn't get as many pieces.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Wh-whatever seemeth to be the problem, young Pwie?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: No, no... Kid's got a point. I never got as many as the rest of you did. This isn't very far out, my dudes. Everyone's supposed to get the same amount.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: *yawn* Guess it's not so fair when someone has more than others.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Was the Happy Closet really happy?
... Their greed was their undoing.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Did you... point out the discrepancy to get them to fight each other?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Yeah. I thought...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... if I pointed it out, they'd start going at each other's throats.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Thought they'd do anything to get one more piece of the clothing 'cuz they're all so selfish.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <Let's take the red heart... and return to Dorothea.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The Happy Closet remained unfurled as Meursault carved the heart out of their chest.
... They've...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... truly given away everything, haven't they?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Don Quixote's sullen gaze lingered on what was left of the Happy Closet. She unpinned a Fixer badge hidden in her jacket and placed it gently on the floor, next to the Closet's remains.
Seeing that, Pwie also took a moment to briefly contemplate what remained of the Closet...
... and after having come to a decision, carefully placed the red handkerchief from the third floor on top of the remains.
... Let's go.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... Oh hello, dear customers...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: You're not looking so good.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Barely... escaped with my life.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: But thanks to that... everything they had... is now mine.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I see that you've... taken the heart, the most precious part... So you were all just... pretending to be uncultured, huh...?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Still... since you were of some help to me... I'll make an exception and.. sell them to you without the markup...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Don't expect any discounts, of course... How dare you take the heart for yourself...?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Have you mind to purchase me? I'm available for a very affordable price.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I'll be waiting.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Why don't you get a move on and find the Happy Closet?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: The way ahead is completely blocked. It does not seem possible to pass through for now.
Will Four-legs be reborn in the form it admired? Will Four-legs... once reborn... still revere One-leg?
No matter whom we were to ask, no one will answer this question.
Of the two lamps, the lit one whispers something. Its lampshade silently swings like a pendulum.
Blink.
Blink.
Bliiiiink.
The lamp seems to blink gratefully.
BlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlink
... Not grateful, got it.
Mere seconds after I laid my hands on the black couch, the distinct shuffling of Furnishings begin creeping up toward us from the shadows.
Furnishings of all kinds creak to life from all around us... and begin to creep in our direction.
Furnishings of all kinds creak to life from all around us... and begin to creep in our direction.
There are a dozen or so legs hanging from the ceiling, all wearing footwear of sorts. A chilling, alien sensation cuts through me.
It's like I'm looking up at the dangling legs of a hanged prisoner.
A display of various shoes.
Pwie doesn't seem to like these.
This display is empty. The label underneath it says [SOLD OUT].
Empty spots in the display stand out to me.
Black shoes with golden highlights.
A display of various, colorful shoes.
Shoes hang from the ceiling.
It's like looking up at the ceiling from the floor.
Elaborate shoes.
If this pair of shoes contains the Golden Hide, it's not obvious. The price is on the lower side.
Hey, man. That coat looks pretty heavy. Why don't you try hanging it from me?
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: (No response. Couldn't be bothered, it seems.)
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Do ya mind, my dudes? It's finally my turn to sunbathe, and you're blocking the light.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: How do you like this bright red cushion I've got? Put me in any room, and I'll fill it with just the appropriate kind of vitality any classy home needs!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: My body is quite cushy. Feel free to take a seat before you go. Hmm... You must be quite tempted to sit on me right about now.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Do you even know what the word Vanitas means? Go away, uneducated fools have no business purchasing me.
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: (No response. Couldn't be bothered, it seems.)
One day I'll get a kewl~ customer who's down for a kewl~ deal.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I'll be worth at least 5,000 Eyeballs now! But for you, I'm available for... an exclusive price of 9,000 Eyeballs. Hmph!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Oh, excuse me...
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Are you really having trouble understanding what "Get lost, fuckwit" means?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: <Some of them don't seem to want to talk to us... if they're even capable of speech.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: As much as I'd like to give them the clothes, there isn't much we can do if their first reaction when we try to talk to them is to attack us... I wonder what other options we have?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hmmmmmmmmm... Quite the pickle indeed... Aha! Perchance, we need only initiate conversation with them as many times as it takes for them to return the favor?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <But Meursault's going to have to go through a gruesome death every time we talk to the wrong Furnishing...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I'faith...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hmm... Ah, right. I think Furnishings in the brighter parts of the hall were more willing to lend us their ear, even if they were a little curt.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I wonder if the light put them in a good mood~?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <The brighter parts?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Aha! Indeed, I too heard the quibble of voices when walking under the sunshine, which were entirely absent while we were in shadows...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Every Furnishing with which communication was possible was exposed to light.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Right... Then the light must be affecting the Furnishings somehow. Let's head down to the Furniture Hall and try again.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Don Quixote won't be able to wear these shoes, but it'd make for a nice gift for her.
In a world where it is so hard to stand on even with two legs, to stand up straight on one leg is a difficult task, regardless of one's nobility.
Whoaaaaa... You guys...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: You have someone so, so... special with you.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: I'm so lucky and grateful... to have a chance to meet someone like that...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Pwie hid behind us, evidently feeling a bit anxious from the overly saccharine reception.
Pwie be their name, kind vendor! Fortunes both ill and good have brought them presently under our care... A bashful young child, I say.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Ah, yes. Please look after them well. Oh, and if you wanted to take a look at the shoes in our store... you'd better make it quick.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: We'll probably be closing down, soon.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Why is that?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Because the Noirs'll probably evict us.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Le Rouge is in decline... our Voice is growing increasingly faint and stretched. The higher Rouges already saw this coming a long time ago.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Lost... and abandoned... all over again.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: But I don't mind, because I know how to get home.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Home?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Yes, home. The place where we all came from. We each had one—and I'm sure you do, too. A place to return to, where people are waiting for you to come back.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Hm! The bus! is our place to return to... Indeed, a bus! so grand and dashing, young Mephi... And within that handsome bus, Lord Red Gaze, a Color Fixer most illustrious... and young Charon await our return.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... Hoh... How peculiar! 'Tis as hazy as though I am speaking of events a millennium ago...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Oh, that's interesting. I thought the residents of the Grand Magasin never talked about their lives before coming here.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: It's true, we do have to forget many, many things to become customers of this department store. I barely remember anything about the life I had before coming here.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: The only memory I have left of the outside world... is the face of someone crying. When the judge's gavel hit the stand and sentenced me to the Sisyphe Penalty, our eyes met—and I saw tears streaming down their cheeks.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Ah, verily... The finality and the weight behind the gavel as it hammered the stand... could bring tears to one's eyes. I recall feeling as though my vision had darkened from the sheer shock.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Where is it that you seek to journey?
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: We're trying to get to the fifth floor.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Ah, perfect... I know how to get to the fifth floor. I can share that secret with you... if you help me find my way home.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: <...! She knows how we can get to the fifth floor?!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: She didn't really say anything of much significance to us when we were helping the Noirs... She was just a sales rep at a shoe store, and that's all she was to us.
If the different choices we've made so far will unlock the fifth floor for us... maybe we can prove Jeanne wrong and bring us to a different end.
<Tell her that we'll help.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... We will help.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Yay... Happy, so happy...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Ever heard the story about the Heartshard Slippers? A living, pulsing pair of shoes embedded with an iridescent red shard of heart.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: They say clapping its heels thrice will guide you home...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: I've been trying to make one, and I have all the materials, but... I've not been able to get my hands on the heart shard.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Where can we get the heart shard...?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... I don't know. There was this bejeweled person who used to manage this floor, and they had a beautiful heart...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: ... But they disappeared some time ago, and haven't been seen in a while.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: They really were a giving soul... I remember how they never hesitated to share their treasures with everyone.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: <A giving soul...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... You will find them in the Furniture Hall.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Oh, really...? Then please, go find the heart shard for me.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: And I'll tell you how to get to the fifth floor.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Hang on a minute... that lamp—he's got way more stuff than we do!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: ... Gimme your toenails, at least. I don't wanna fall behind.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: And give up that pull switch, too.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: N-now hold your damn horses, everyone. This pull switch didn't come from—
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: But he doesn't get to finish his sentence as the Furnishings begin to pile onto each other.
The racket eventually dies down, and all movements cease. Only a pile of broken Furnishings remain.
... Ooh... A glittering heart. It's still beating, too.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: With this... I can fashion the slippers that will take me home.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: And you'll also tell us how to reach the fifth floor, yes?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Mhm... I go home, and you go to the fifth floor.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Follow me.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Here, here.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: ... You hear it too, don't you?
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: H-hear what...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The whisper guiding us home. Don't you hear it? The heartbeat from the shoes—it's quickening.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Now, this spot... is where I'll clap the heels together. Three times.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: *tap* *tap* *tap*
As the heels of the shoes struck each other...
An opening appeared in the wall, leading somewhere beyond.
Art thou certain... that this truly be thy homeward road?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Mhm. This... is the Lost Child Center.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: A gathering place... for children... lost on their way home...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: I need the heart of the giving soul to go home...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Can you please let me know when you find it?
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: The heart is likely in the Furniture Hall on the same floor, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I'll be waiting.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Something resembling a pair of shoes was placed neatly atop the Abnormality's remains.
There you go, the key... to the fifth floor...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: ... You came here knowing that you'd die?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Ah... What a sweet scent.
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: I will... go back to the grave... with the lost... children...
texts.speaker: Dorothea

texts.text: Welcome! Come right in. Excuse the mess; we've only just opened—so we've been repainting the interior.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: As you can see, the wallpaper won't stick smoothly when too many Noirs keep moving beneath it. The finish is far from the ideal interior design, too.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Our brand is, well, brand new. Despite that, we recently completed a successful collaboration with Briand, the model on the sixth floor.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: If I can ensure this establishment opens without issues, it might become the best Handbags Hall that's ever been erected by the Rouges!
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Ahh... Papering the wall... what a pleasing endeavor...
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Um... 'twould seem the path toward the escalator hath been blocked...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: And why should that matter? All that matters is how perfectly smooth the wallpaper will look once it's up on the walls.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: She's really absorbed in her work.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Let's try speaking to the salesperson next to this one...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh, well. We'll need to hire a new clerk. I suppose I shouldn't assign the next one to wallpapering...
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Please call me up if you need help finding anything. We've just opened, so our handbags collection is brand-new.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Don't hesitate to try them and see how they look on you.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... Welcome.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: You...
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... This one seems to be my follower.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: But of course! The instant I beheld you, all the blood vessels in my body started to thrum for no one else but you. Your presence fills me with rapture...
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Every Rouge who calls themselves faithful will cherish you, worship you, and offer everything at their disposal only for you.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... I know.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Honored strangers, please care for our most precious one with the utmost devotion.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: That we shall. We have even shod Young Pwie in a pair of shoes.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... I have another request. Renée often mutters to herself while staring at the wall. A little self-directed discourse is harmless, of course; every handbag designer is fated to contemplate the great dilemma of design in the marrow of their bones.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: But Renée, you see...
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: She likes to press her face against the wall and mutter without end... It's simply incessant. I'd like to stop being an unwilling audience to her hair-raising antics.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: At first, I thought she was taking a bite or two out of the wall, unable to contain her hunger... but no. She's simply rubbing her face against the wall. Never stops.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Would you be so kind as to inspect what she sees in the wall... and who she's speaking to?
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Once that's dealt with... I believe I can clear the path leading to the escalator.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: <There's a voice... coming from inside the wall...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I've been following the sunlight faithfully from the first moment it reached out to this place.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: That's why the Rouges and the Noirs are both fools for obsessing over the Golden Hide without a care for the future. The collapse of the department store was sealed... when the cracks first appeared on the walls.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: If you're going to kick me out of the shop... at least let me bury myself in this sunlit wall. Let me remain in the light forever...
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: ... What do you say, strangers? Ought I show this thing mercy?
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: I will lend my ears to your judgment.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: I'll bury you inside the wall. It will be... your final piece of interior work.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Thank you. I'll wait in here, basking in sunshine, until everything inevitably dries up...
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: That's a no, Renée.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: I can't let a vile Néant live.
texts.speaker: Le Rouge Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... You do that. The sunlight... never scorns those who do not follow it, anyway.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: All it wants is to wait... and to embrace.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: ... It's not long now, my children.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Soon, you will be born as the most precious and beloved beings in this department store...
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... Hello. Do you happen to know how to get to the escalator of this floor?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Whether or not I know, it would do you little good. Getting on an escalator only makes noise.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: That vulgar grinding of metal gnaws at the delicate minds of my unfinished children—the more beautiful the being, the more sensitive it is. And they are nothing if not sensitive.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Children, thou sayest...? Where be these children?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: They will wake soon. My masterpieces, born only of this department store's golden materials.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: This is my 68th attempt. Surely it will succeed. 68 is an excellent number.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: I don't... care about that.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: What I want to know is... how to get to the escalator.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... What a tiresome little abomination.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Well, this might prove convenient. Bring me golden materials from the roaming mannequins if you wish to know the way there.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Get me enough of what I ask for, and I may tell you.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: <... Let's do as he says.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We brought the—
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ahh, yes! At last!
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: <... He didn't even let us finish before grabbing them.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Golden Eye, Golden Tooth... and Golden Hair.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Now, my masterpieces... You may open your 68th eyes.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Eeeek! Those uggos are burning my eyes! Shield my eyes, Papa...
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: Are we... the best pieces now...?
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: The children he meant... were those bags?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Who might these "uggos" be?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I think they mean us.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Just another variation of the unsolicited fashion advice we've been getting since entering this department store...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Come, I shall grant you the special honor of laying eyes upon my children.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: This fabric was sewn stitch by stitch by my own hand. It's tough and resilient.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Mmhmm! My skin's tough. It never tears.
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: And this curve was modeled after the neckline of a sixth-floor model—the model who drew the eyes of so many.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: I'm worth more than I was yesterday, aren't I, Papa?
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: Of course. Your value rises with every passing day.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: And this child's eye is made from a shard taken from a full-length mirror—the very same one cherished by the customer who wore the most expensive attire in all of the Grand Magasin. It is saturated with that customer's longing.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Papa, why don't those things covet us when they look at us?
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: Shh, child. These customers are not worthy of possessing you. Merely being permitted to look is more than they deserve.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... Did you hear my child? And that thing you're traveling with is... simply ghastly. Do ensure it never associates with my children again.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: You're not... "the best."
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: I've seen fabric that shines brighter than this.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: No. That's... impossible. Brighter than this?
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Yeah, a bolt of Golden Fabric woven to rip me apart. It's the same fabric wrapped around that big one's fists.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: ... You possess fabric made of gold?
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... Yes.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: For what felt like minutes, the designer stared blankly at the Golden Fabric wrapped around Meursault's gauntlet, disbelief written across his face.
How could I have failed to notice that? That light inside your bag, it's... Fabric woven from exceptionally pure Golden Thread... Magnificent...
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: But... I heard that the Golden Thread can be woven only from fabled materials now only passed down as tales and legends... That, even if you were to acquire them somehow, it would take countless seasons of waiting on B2 to truly complete it...
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: It's the reason... I have never once seen anyone wear Golden Fabric.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... So the materials composing my children... were not the finest this time either.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: All of this is pointless... if you're not the best...
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Ugly! Anything that isn't made from Golden Thread is ugly!
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: ... Did we fail again, Papa?
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: The best... When?
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: The handbag designer slowly began to strangle the bags he had called his children.
What is this heinous treachery?! To take the lives of those who call thee father...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: No, they're no children of mine...! My children are only the very best, and these are anything but!
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: What... what madness this be...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: You should have been born with every part made of glittering, golden material...
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Ghk... uggo. Ug... go...
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: I... don't want... to die... Pa... pa...
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: The best... when? The... best...
texts.speaker: The Designer's Chef D'oeuvre

texts.text: Don Quixote raised her lance and charged at the designer, but...
There is something more important than surviving, children. And it is... to remain beautiful.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Ghh...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... her attack amounted to nothing. Only Meursault was capable of causing physical harm in the Symbolic.
Wait just a little longer. I'll find something even more precious than the Golden Fabric... And with it, my hands will birth the greatest masterpiece the Grand Magasin has ever known...!
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: How... could one be so wicked...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... All those precious materials that went into creating them, and they still weren't good enough for you. Just how... do you intend to make anything finer than the Golden Fabric?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Perhaps the answer to that lies in the deepest underground, beneath even the Nest where threads are spun... Yes, where they say the Rouges' most precious hides are tanned and processed.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: It has to be true... The Rouge I used as my firstborn's handle gasped that rumor with its dying breath.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: Besides, after the thread comes the hide. Such is the way of fashion.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: No matter how many seasons it takes... I will descend. I'll get my hands on the finest hide out there... and create the best children I have ever had!
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: ... I doubt anything we say will reach you now.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: But perhaps... your "most perfect" child... was the very first bag you ever made.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Nonsense. Go, go take the escalator... I won't bother seeing you out.
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: The 69th attempt will surely, surely...
texts.speaker: Le Noir Handbags Hall Designer

texts.text: <... We should go.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Why did he abandon them?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Apparently they didn't shine as brightly as he wanted. I don't think he knows that nothing in the world can shine as brightly as his expectations.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... You can't abandon me.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Because I can't afford to stop... if I'm to reach what I want.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: The Manager... won't abandon you.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What about you?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: I know naught of thy desires, Young Pwie... But pray, endeavor with all thy heart, and thy dream shall bear fruit!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... I dunno if it's my "dream." I don't even know what "dream" is.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: A dream, Young Pwie, is the roaring fire that fuels the spirit of adventure! Verily, though one might dream nightmares of treble dread that tarry one's feet...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Yet if thou endurest every trial and chargest ever onward... then thou shalt surely reach what thou desirest!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: What are your dreams...?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Ahem! 'Tis to become a Fixer most valiant and ...! Uh, though at present, I suppose our dream is to reach the highest floor of this department store. However, that will come to pass only after we take thee to the fifth floor, Young Pwie...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I don't get it.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: There isn't an "after" once you take me there.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: You have to stay with me on the fifth floor.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: <... Looks like little Pwie doesn't wanna say goodbye.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Young Pwie... we too would be loath to part with thee—alas, we cannot linger on the fifth floor for all eternity.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Why...? Is it because you miss "Lord Red Gaze"... and... the person you call "Young Charon"?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Hmm... that is not entirely wrong, forsooth...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... Can't you just stay with me?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: We have a lot of things to do outside this department store. So... I don't think we can stay with you forever, Pwie.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Then...
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: If you didn't have those "things to do"... we'd stay together?
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: I doubt such a day shall ever arrive...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: But should it arrive, then thou canst accompany us and remain by our side instead!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I couldn't say for sure whether Don Quixote's answer was good enough for them, but Pwie asked no more questions and quietly took their place behind Meursault.
So you found the Voice, too.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: It's so very warm... isn't it?
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Aah... I feel I could remain like this forever.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: I want to wedge my whole body into this crack and stay there, listening to the Voice and basking in the warmth until the day arrives...
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: ... It seemeth our words do not at all reach them.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: She rubs herself against the wall, oblivious to the dead flesh sloughing off her face and ears from the friction.
This one is not my follower.

<color=#ebcaa2>Say, have you ever thought about it?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Death, I mean, and the aversion to it. It's a perfectly natural response, isn't it?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>That's why there are numerous requirements to satisfy before one can purchase Canned Experiences containing cruelty and violence.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Now then, some food for thought—have you ever wondered why sexuality, like death, provokes similar aversion and censorship?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>There are many possible answers, I'm sure... But here's mine.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>We're afraid of and revolted by both procreation and death because... at the end of the day, birthing something is no different from killing it.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>I say inviting someone into this world—forcing them to be born—is pure violence, an act as grossly irresponsible as murder.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>So, there it is. Dragging someone into the world unawares, and removing them from it—neither has an ounce of respect for their volition.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>They're fundamentally the same thing.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>Humans know this by instinct. But that is precisely what causes the pain of dissonance. Because it clashes with our nature, which is hardwired to do anything for the preservation of our species.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>This is why the ideas of birth and death are both so terrifying and alluring at the same time. It's simply how we're made—to be human is to be tempted to play with what is taboo.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>The Rouges are perpetually excreting. Birthing.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>The Noirs want no part in any of that. They don't want to give birth to anything, nor do they wish to experience death.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>And... Ta-da! This is what the Grand Magasin is to me:</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>A place where desire swells and bursts with no restraint, put on exhibit. Everything is for sale here.</color>
